transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. Um, I guess what finally pushed me to come in... well, it's probably nothing major, but I've been having a little trouble just... staying in my chair? I hope that doesn't sound too silly. 

It's just, lately I keep getting up during things where I really know I should stay put. Like during our sprint planning meetings at work, or even important personal things, like mortgage calls. I'll just suddenly feel like I absolutely need to go grab a glass of water right that second, or I'll decide I have to check something in the other room. 

It's a little embarrassing, honestly, because I'm a professional and I know how it looks, but I just get a bit restless, I suppose. Is that... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing people usually come to see you for?
When you get up in those moments, is it because you feel you must do something to prevent something bad from happening?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. Um, I'm sorry if I made it sound that intense! I don't ever feel like something bad is going to happen. It's really just... well, it's more like a physical urge just to move a little bit. 

Like, my legs just feel like they need a quick stretch, or I'll just suddenly think, "Oh, I should grab my coffee mug from the kitchen." It's not driven by any kind of worry or fear at all. I hope that's a good thing? I just get a little fidgety, I suppose. Am I answering your question right? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or high, even when other people thought it was excessive?

Oh, gosh, no. I don't think I've ever felt like that. I mean, I try to be upbeat and positive, especially at work with my team, but definitely never anything that people would call excessive or... or high. 

I hope that's okay? I really wouldn't want anyone to think I was acting out of control or anything like that. I'm actually pretty level-headed most of the time! Just... a bit bouncy sometimes, I guess. Is that what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not misunderstanding the question.
Did you have this same kind of trouble sitting still when you were a child?

Um, well... yes, I suppose I did. I hope that's not too terrible to admit. But, um, I do remember back in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes have to move my desk a little bit, or... or they'd have to gently remind me to stay in my seat. 

I guess I was just a really eager kid? I was always popping up to see things, or I'd get so excited I'd start talking before they called on me. And I'd kind of rush through my worksheets, even when I totally understood the material, just because I wanted to get to the next thing. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be a bad student or anything! I always wanted to do well and make the teachers happy. I was just... a little overly enthusiastic, maybe? Does that sound like what you're asking about? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a complete terror as a child!
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I worry a lot. I mean, I care about things, of course! I care about doing a good job on my projects at work, and making sure my team is supported, but... it's not like a constant, heavy worry. 

I don't just sit around stressing about things for no reason. I try to be really proactive and just tackle whatever needs to be done. If I'm thinking about something a lot, it's usually just because I'm trying to figure out the best way to solve a problem, not because I'm anxious about it. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm, like, falling apart over every little detail. I think I handle everyday stuff pretty well! Is that... is that a helpful answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
